```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc"
st <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_stats.tsv"))
pts <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_points.tsv"))
fun <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_funnel.tsv"))
PAPER <- "Paper's cutoff"; BEFORE <- "Before FDR"; AFTER <- "After FDR"
SET_ORDER <- c(PAPER, BEFORE, AFTER)
tpl <- function(x) sub("hr", " hr", x)
hn <- pts[set == BEFORE & tp == "6hr" & gene == "HNRNPK" & variant_qual == "chr9:83980154:C>T"]
```

This page compares **read-based isoLASER** without the clustering filter
([FDR page](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html)) with GTEx v8 Cerebellum sQTLs. The
[comparison with the filter](isolaser_gtex_comparison_reads10.html) remains as an earlier setup.

As before, we compare our allelic splicing effects (isoLASER ΔPSI) with GTEx v8
Cerebellum sQTL effects (beta), as in the right panel of
[Fig. 3e of the isoLASER paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6).
We use each event's **skipping junction**, whose usage falls when the exonic
part is included, so a **negative correlation** is expected.

# How pairs were matched

The matching is unchanged:

- **Variant and gene:** the same SNV (position, REF and ALT; isoLASER's
  0-based position + 1 = GTEx's) tested for the same Ensembl gene in GTEx.
- **GTEx data:** full Cerebellum summary statistics, every tested association
  at any p-value.
- **Event:** the exonic part must form an annotated exon-skipping or
  alternative-splice-site event, and the GTEx junction must be exactly that
  event's skipping junction.
- **Points:** each point is one **pair**: an isoLASER association (variant ×
  exonic part) and its matched GTEx skipping junction, at one timepoint.

Our associations come in three sets:

- **Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` label and pooled ΔPSI, as in the
  paper, from the read-based run's joint output. It does not depend on our family
  rules, so it is the same set as on the page with the clustering filter.
- **Before FDR:** this run's screen. The donors are panel-heterozygous with
  ≥ 10 reads, with ≥ 20 reads over those donors, `cis`, |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10 and part
  ≥ 10 bp; variants with another candidate variant within 30 bp are kept.
- **After FDR:** this run's screen plus permutation BH q < 0.05 within each
  timepoint, as on [this run's FDR page](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html).

**Example, HNRNPK.** The C>T variant (chr9:83980154, 0-based) and the 34-base
exonic part (gold) form an alternative splice site. GTEx measures the
skipping junction (blue), which jumps over the part. At 6 hours, ALT changes
part inclusion by `r sprintf("%+.1f", 100*hn$dpsi)` percentage points in this
run. GTEx's beta for the skipping junction is `r sprintf("%+.2f", hn$slope)`:
opposite signs, as expected.

![](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/comparable_event_example_skipping.png)

```{r funnel}
f <- fun[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
             `Our associations (SNVs)`=reported_snv_associations, `Same variant and gene tested in GTEx`=tested_in_gtex,
             `Plotted pairs`=plotted, Genes=genes)]
knitr::kable(f, align="llrrrr")
```

**Our associations (SNVs)**: variant × exonic part associations with a
single-base variant at that timepoint. **Same variant and gene tested in
GTEx**: of those, the ones whose variant GTEx Cerebellum tests for the same
gene. **Plotted pairs**: association × matched GTEx skipping junction.

As in the run with the clustering filter, every SNV in the before- and after-FDR sets is in our
genotype panel, so most are tested in GTEx. Before FDR,
`r paste(range(round(100 * fun[set == BEFORE, tested_in_gtex / reported_snv_associations])), collapse="&ndash;")`%
are tested; after FDR,
`r paste(range(round(100 * fun[set == AFTER, tested_in_gtex / reported_snv_associations])), collapse="&ndash;")`%.

# Result

![](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/fig3e_style.png)

[Download PDF](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/fig3e_style.pdf)

```{r stats}
s <- dcast(st[subset %in% c("all", "GTEx p < 1e-5")], set + tp ~ subset, value.var=c("n", "expected_sign", "pearson_r", "pearson_p"))
s <- s[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
           `Pairs`=n_all, `All: R (p)`=fifelse(is.na(pearson_r_all), "too few",
             sprintf("%.2f (%s)", pearson_r_all, vapply(pearson_p_all, function(x) format(signif(x, 2)), ""))),
           `All: expected sign`=sprintf("%d/%d", expected_sign_all, n_all),
           `GTEx p < 1e-5: expected sign`=fifelse(is.na(`n_GTEx p < 1e-5`), "none", sprintf("%d/%d", `expected_sign_GTEx p < 1e-5`, `n_GTEx p < 1e-5`)))]
knitr::kable(s, align="llrrrr")
```

**R (p)**: Pearson correlation of our ΔPSI with GTEx's beta, with its p-value.
A negative R is expected. **Expected sign**: pairs where our ΔPSI and GTEx's
beta have opposite signs. **GTEx p < 1e-5**: only pairs where GTEx itself has
strong evidence.

## Direction where GTEx is significant

As on the original page, we take pairs where GTEx is significant (nominal
p < 0.05, the blue points). A pair is **consistent** when our ΔPSI and GTEx's
beta have opposite signs. A binomial test asks whether the share of consistent
pairs differs from 50%. These definitions are our own; the paper reports only
the correlation.

```{r consistency}
bt <- function(d) {
  k <- sum(d$dpsi * d$slope < 0); n <- nrow(d)
  data.table(Pairs=n, Consistent=k, `Consistent (%)`=if (n) round(100 * k / n) else NA_real_,
             `Binomial p, two-sided`=if (n) signif(binom.test(k, n)$p.value, 2) else NA_real_,
             `Binomial p, one-sided`=if (n) signif(binom.test(k, n, alternative="greater")$p.value, 2) else NA_real_)
}
cons <- rbindlist(lapply(SET_ORDER, function(x) {
  blue <- pts[set == x & pval_nominal < 0.05 & dpsi != 0]
  once <- blue[, .(dpsi=mean(dpsi), slope=slope[1]), by=.(Gene_name, variant_qual, exonic_part, phenotype_id)]
  rbind(blue[order(tp), bt(.SD), by=.(Timepoint=tpl(tp))],
        data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, every point", bt(blue)),
        data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, each pair once", bt(once)))[, Set := x]
}))
knitr::kable(cons[, c("Set", setdiff(names(cons), "Set")), with=FALSE], align="llrrrrr")
```

**Pairs**: association × GTEx skipping junction with GTEx p < 0.05.
**Consistent**: pairs with opposite signs. **Two-sided p**: is the share
different from 50%. **One-sided p**: is it above 50%, the direction expected.
**Every point** counts each timepoint's points, so a pair called at several
timepoints counts several times. **Each pair once** uses each pair's mean ΔPSI
over the timepoints where it is called.

# All 13 GTEx brain tissues

```{r brain_setup}
bs <- fread(file.path(A, "brain_tissues_stats.tsv")); bf <- fread(file.path(A, "brain_tissues_funnel.tsv"))
bp <- fread(file.path(A, "brain_tissues_points.tsv"))
tname <- function(x) gsub("_", " ", sub("^Brain_", "", x))
rp2 <- function(r, p) fifelse(is.na(r), "too few", sprintf("%.2f (%s)", r, vapply(p, function(x) if (is.na(x)) "NA" else format(signif(x, 2)), "")))
kn <- function(k, n) fifelse(n == 0, "none", sprintf("%d/%d", k, n))
n_assoc <- bf[, associations[1], by=tp][, sum(V1)]
full <- bs[scope == "each pair once" & subset == "all" & data_type == "full"]
```

Here the comparison is repeated in all 13 GTEx v8 brain tissues, for the
after-FDR set at the effect cutoff of our report: BH q < 0.05, `cis` and
\|ΔPSI\| ≥ 0.05 (`r n_assoc` associations over 0, 1 and 6 hours). The matching is
the same as above: the same SNV and gene, and the GTEx junction must be the
annotated event's skipping junction.

- **Full** (9 tissues): GTEx's full summary statistics, every tested
  association at any p-value, as for Cerebellum above.
- **Significant pairs only** (Amygdala, Anterior cingulate cortex BA24, Spinal
  cord cervical c-1 and Substantia nigra): only GTEx's significant pairs are
  available on the cluster. Only pairs GTEx calls significant can match, so these
  rows are not comparable with the full tissues.

```{r brain_table}
once <- dcast(bs[scope == "each pair once"], tissue + data_type ~ subset, value.var=c("n", "genes", "expected_sign", "pearson_r", "pearson_p"))
tested <- bf[, .(tested=sum(tested_in_gtex), total=sum(associations)), by=tissue]
once <- merge(once, tested, by="tissue")
once <- once[order(data_type != "full", tissue)]
knitr::kable(once[, .(Tissue=tname(tissue), `GTEx data`=data_type,
  `Associations tested in GTEx`=sprintf("%d/%d", tested, total), Pairs=n_all, Genes=genes_all,
  `R (p)`=rp2(pearson_r_all, pearson_p_all), `Expected sign`=kn(expected_sign_all, n_all),
  `GTEx p < 0.05: expected sign`=kn(`expected_sign_GTEx p < 0.05`, `n_GTEx p < 0.05`))], align="llrrrrrr")
```

Across the 9 full tissues, R is between `r sprintf("%.2f", min(full$pearson_r))` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(full$pearson_r))`, and `r sum(full$expected_sign)` of `r sum(full$n)` pairs (summed over
tissues) have the expected sign. This matches Cerebellum above: the same few associations
(`r paste(sort(unique(bp[role == "skipping", gene])), collapse=", ")`) match in every brain tissue, and their
effects agree with GTEx in direction in all of them.

**Associations tested in GTEx**: association × timepoint rows whose variant
GTEx reports for the same gene in that tissue, of all rows in the set. For the
significant-pairs tissues this means a significant pair in the gene.
**Pairs**: association × matched GTEx skipping junction, each pair once, with
its mean ΔPSI over the timepoints where the association is reported. **R (p)**:
Pearson correlation of our ΔPSI with GTEx's beta; a negative R is expected.
**Expected sign**: pairs where our ΔPSI and GTEx's beta have opposite signs.
**GTEx p < 0.05**: the same, for pairs with GTEx nominal p < 0.05. The tissues
share many GTEx donors, so the rows are not independent.

```{r brain_tp}
pt <- bs[scope != "each pair once" & subset == "all"][order(data_type != "full", tissue, scope)]
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(pt[, .(Tissue=tname(tissue), `GTEx data`=data_type, Timepoint=tpl(scope), Pairs=n,
  `R (p)`=rp2(pearson_r, pearson_p), `Expected sign`=kn(expected_sign, n))]),
  rownames=FALSE, filter="top", options=list(pageLength=13, scrollX=TRUE))
```

The same statistics for each timepoint separately. The matched pairs, with
every tissue, are in [this table](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/brain_tissues_points.tsv).

# Compared with the run with the clustering filter

```{r vs_base}
stb <- fread("docs/assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10/fig3e_style_stats.tsv")[subset == "all"]
two <- rbind(stb[, run := "base"], st[subset == "all"][, run := "here"], fill=TRUE)
w <- dcast(two, set + tp ~ run, value.var=c("n", "expected_sign", "pearson_r", "pearson_p"))
rp <- function(r, p) fifelse(is.na(r), "too few", sprintf("%.2f (%s)", r, vapply(p, function(x) if (is.na(x)) "NA" else format(signif(x, 2)), "")))
knitr::kable(w[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
  `With filter: R (p)`=rp(pearson_r_base, pearson_p_base), `With filter: expected sign`=sprintf("%d/%d", expected_sign_base, n_base),
  `This run: R (p)`=rp(pearson_r_here, pearson_p_here), `This run: expected sign`=sprintf("%d/%d", expected_sign_here, n_here))],
  align="llrrrr")
```

**With filter** is the [read-based isoLASER's comparison](isolaser_gtex_comparison_reads10.html); **This
run** is this page. Columns as in the result table above. Before FDR this run has
`r st[subset == "all" & set == BEFORE, sum(n)]` pairs against `r stb[set == BEFORE, sum(n)]`, with
`r round(100 * st[subset == "all" & set == BEFORE, sum(expected_sign) / sum(n)])`% of the expected sign against
`r round(100 * stb[set == BEFORE, sum(expected_sign) / sum(n)])`%; after FDR,
`r st[subset == "all" & set == AFTER, sum(n)]` pairs against `r stb[set == AFTER, sum(n)]`, with
`r st[subset == "all" & set == AFTER, sum(expected_sign)]` and `r stb[set == AFTER, sum(expected_sign)]` of the expected sign.

Dropping the clustering filter changes little here. Before FDR it adds a few pairs,
and the correlation stays negative at every timepoint (similar or slightly
stronger than with the filter); after FDR the pairs are the same, because the gained
associations, all in the MHC, have no matched GTEx pair. The paper's-cutoff rows
are the same set in both runs.

# Data

```{r points}
d <- pts[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp, gene), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp), Gene=gene,
  Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part, `GTEx junction`=paste0(intron_start_0, "-", intron_end_0),
  `Our dPSI`=round(dpsi, 3), `Our BH q`=signif(q_bh, 2), `GTEx beta`=signif(slope, 3), `GTEx p`=signif(pval_nominal, 2))]
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE))
```

**Variant**: isoLASER's 0-based position. **GTEx junction**: 0-based,
half-open intron coordinates. **Our BH q** is blank for the paper's-cutoff set,
which has no permutation test. Download the
[points](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/fig3e_style_points.tsv) and
[statistics](assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/fig3e_style_stats.tsv).

Reproduce with `long_read_RNA/10.isolaser_permutation/54.family_rules_gtex.sbatch`
(`ADAPTIVE_RULE=reads10nc`): `27.gtex_fdr_comparison.py --prepare-full-cerebellum` and
`34.extract_full_cerebellum.R`, each for the after-FDR set and with `--before-fdr`;
then `36.plot_fig3e_style.R` and `29.gtex_comparable_examples.R --skipping`. The
paper's-cutoff set is the filtered run's, read without being changed. Everything else
is written under `out/adaptive_reads10nc/` and `docs/assets/isolaser_gtex_reads10nc/`.
